moves.critique: Strongest feature: Carrier identifies a comparative inference: passion narratives, filial divinity, victory over death, benefits shared with worshippers, and stories located in earthly history could place Jesus within a savior-deity reference class, thereby challenging an exceptionalist historical prior. Principal limitation: The class remains underdemonstrated because no named deities, dates, sources, counterexamples, or stable criteria establish that every member possessed these features while being nonexistent; local differences do not repair the compression. Live burden: To make the historicization precedent probative, Carrier must name comparators, distinguish borrowing from development, justify class boundaries, and show that similarities predict fabrication more strongly than they predict mythologizing a person. Locked score: The frozen pattern reflects forceful burden contact and responsiveness, alongside weaker evidential warrant, calibration, definitional precision, and moderate inferential coherence.

Strongest feature: Carrier constructs a Jewish alternative from Philo’s firstborn son, divine image, creation agent, and celestial high priest, relating these attributes to Pauline and Hebrews language, thus supplying a preexistent model beyond biographical silence. Principal limitation: The argument compresses Philo’s angel, Paul’s Christ, descent, incarnation, death, and resurrection into one identification although the parallels alone do not independently establish that authors describe the same being or sequence. Live burden: Carrier must provide passages, separate titles from analogies, date the traditions, and demonstrate that celestial identification explains the earliest evidence better than exaltation of a historical claimant rather than merely accommodating it. Locked score: The frozen pattern favors responsiveness and relevance, preserves respectable coherence, clarity, and calibration, but exposes markedly thinner warrant for the identity bridge.
